implementation_notes: Swift protocols with associated types give real abstraction; use `some View`-style opaque return types (primary associated types, Swift 5.7) to keep the abstraction from leaking. Access control is the encapsulation lever: `private(set)` on stored properties plus `internal` types keeps implementations out of the module's public surface.
idiom_name: protocol + primary associated types (some P) + access-level-based encapsulation
pitfalls: Existential types (`any P`) need explicit `any` from Swift 5.7 and lose static dispatch.
Reference types default to class semantics; `struct` value semantics usually give better substitutability.
Open classes invite LSP violations; prefer composition over subclassing for reuse.
